# RESULTS_B - Data-quality layer (generated by report.py)

## Read this first (honest limits)
* Data source of every number below: **SYNTHETIC (generator in project_b/synth_311.py)**. The build sandbox could not reach NYC Open Data, so the numbers come from `project_b/synth_311.py`. To reproduce on the real 2023 data: `python -m project_b.fetch_311` then `python -m project_b.profile_raw --csv project_b/data/nyc311_2023.csv && python -m project_b.evaluate --csv project_b/data/nyc311_2023.csv`. Expect lower recall and more false alarms on real data.
* Synthetic assumptions that flatter detectors: templated resolution text (easy for rules/classifier), clean zip/borough tables, injector and detectors written by the same author. Legit repeat complaints (1.5% of rows) and natural nulls (3% lat/lon, 1% zip) ARE modelled so false alarms are measurable.
* LLM review (family c): **NOT RUN** (no GEMINI_API_KEY). Cost is projected from real prompt text; detection columns need `python -m project_b.evaluate --llm`.
* Cost = measured single-core CPU seconds x $0.04/vCPU-hour (assumption); LLM = Gemini list price assumptions in `project_a/llm.py` (verify).

## Task 6 - scale and design (50M rows/day, 120 customers)
* Cheap stage: 0.53 core-hours/day = $0.02/day. Daily baseline refit for 120 customers: 0.07 core-hours.
* LLM: hybrid sampling = 10,000 calls/day, ~$15/day; reviewing every row = ~$1,972/day. Free tier cannot serve this; need paid quota or a smaller self-hosted model, with ~21 calls/min peak.
* What changes at scale: (1) per-customer schema mapping becomes an LLM-once-per-customer onboarding step (120 calls) that emits column maps and per-customer rule configs reviewed by a human; (2) thresholds (null rate, repeat-gap, zip map) must be learned per customer, not global; (3) switch to streaming micro-batches with vectorised/columnar engines (Arrow/Polars) and horizontal sharding by customer; (4) LLM only on gated rows, with caching of identical row-templates and a hard per-customer budget; (5) alert de-duplication/batch-level minimum counts to control alert fatigue; (6) rules for structural problems (p01-p05, p08, p09) stay rules - they were 100% and cheapest.
